name: Treaty of Jaffa 1229
summary: Frederick II, Holy Roman Emperor, leads the Sixth Crusade (1228–1229) while under excommunication. Rather than fighting, he negotiates the Treaty of Jaffa with Ayyubid Sultan al-Kamil (who wanted Frederick's diplomatic support against his own relatives): Jerusalem, Bethlehem, Nazareth, and a corridor to the sea are returned to Christian control for ten years. Frederick crowns himself King of Jerusalem in the Church of the Holy Sepulchre (March 18, 1229), the patriarch of Jerusalem refusing to participate. The deal outraged the Military Orders and the papacy; Teutonic Knight opponents threw offal at Frederick's departure from Acre.

_quarry.structural_significance: Recovers Jerusalem diplomatically without military force, the only successful diplomatic crusade; Frederick's self-coronation asserts imperial independence from the papacy; the ten-year truce allows Latin presence but no military buildup; Jerusalem is retaken by the Khwarazmians in 1244
